tool_input.command: f=$(node -p "require.resolve('react-hook-form')" 2>/dev/null); echo "$f"; d=$(dirname "$f"); ls "$d" | head; grep -n "\"version\"" node_modules/react-hook-form/package.json 2>/dev/null; grep -rn "_f.onChange\|onChange: " node_modules/react-hook-form/dist/index.esm.mjs 2>/dev/null | head -20; cat src/lib/authorization.ts | head -40
tool_input.description: Check react-hook-form version and onChange handling; read ROLES
Rewrite hook and component to use shared form components

result:
Both rule violations are fixed in the two new files. I didn't run tests, lint, or the app, as you asked.

- **Notifications moved into the hook.** `api/update-user-role.ts` now calls `useNotifications` and shows the "User Role Updated" success message in `onSuccess`, next to the existing cache invalidation. `components/update-user-role.tsx` no longer imports `useNotifications`.
- **Raw select replaced.** The component now uses `Form` (with the zod schema and `defaultValues`) and the `Select` field from `@/components/ui/form`. Changing the value calls `requestSubmit()` on the form, which runs the mutation.

Behaviour changes to check:
- **Current user:** the component renders the role as plain text instead of a disabled select. `Select` has no `disabled` prop, so I didn't add one.
- **Pending state:** the select isn't disabled while the request is in flight, which the old code did. Disabling it through `register` would reset its value in react-hook-form, so I left it out.
- **Accessibility:** the old `aria-label="User role"` is gone, and `Select` renders no visible label here. The select is still wrapped in a label element, but it has no text, so screen readers may announce it unnamed. Passing `label="User role"` would fix that but adds visible text to each row.
- **Auto-submit timing:** `requestSubmit()` is called from the field's `onChange`. I'm relying on react-hook-form storing the new value before that callback runs. I couldn't verify this without installing dependencies, which I didn't do.

The notification and form patterns in the other existing user and discussion components still call `useNotifications` from components. I left them alone since you asked only for the new code to be fixed.

Nothing has been committed.
